item.text: {"evidence_refs":["fit_0","fit_1","fit_3","fit_6","fit_9","fit_10","fit_12","fit_15","fit_18","fit_21","fit_24","fit_27","fit_30","fit_33","dev_0","dev_6","dev_12","dev_18","observed_A_0","observed_A_8","observed_A_16","observed_A_24","observed_B_0","observed_B_4"],"experiments":[{"h":0.5,"history":[1,0,0,0],"purpose":"At an unseen drive, compare an old isolated pulse against the matched recent-pulse condition to measure temporal weighting.","u":0.3},{"h":0.5,"history":[0,0,0,1],"purpose":"Matched recent isolated pulse; test whether equal pulse magnitude at different ages gives different response.","u":0.3},{"h":1.5,"history":[1,0,0,0],"purpose":"Repeat old pulse after a longer wait to test memory decay and direct wait dependence.","u":0.3},{"h":1.5,"history":[0,0,0,1],"purpose":"Matched long-wait recent pulse to separate pulse-age from waiting-time effects.","u":0.3}],"exposed_inputs":["u","h","history","times"],"expression":"a+b*u+c*h+d*memory","measurement_requests":["Use four repeats per condition and report raw response values."],"parameters":[{"dimension":[0,1],"initial":0,"lower":-3,"name":"a","upper":3},{"dimension":[0,1],"initial":1,"lower":-3,"name":"b","upper":3},{"dimension":[-1,1],"initial":-0.2,"lower":-2,"name":"c","upper":2},{"dimension":[0,1],"initial":0.5,"lower":-3,"name":"d","upper":3},{"dimension":[1,0],"initial":1,"lower":0.1,"name":"tau","upper":8}],"quantities":[{"expression":"sum(history*exp(times/tau))","interpretation":"Dimensionless exponentially age-weighted prior drive summary; the fixed interval duration is one second and is absorbed into fitted coefficient d.","name":"memory"}],"rationale":"The old global linear fit has poor fit and dev errors, and matched u,h contrasts show history matters (dev_0 versus dev_6). Equal-sum histories produce distinct responses: at u=.65,h=.5, recent isolated pulse exceeds the old pulse (observed_A_8 vs observed_A_0), while alternating histories also differ strongly by order (observed_A_24 vs observed_A_16). This motivates a temporally weighted memory summary. Positive versus negative constant history responses are markedly separated at both waits (dev_0/dev_6 and dev_12/dev_18), supporting a memory contribution; their change with h supports retaining direct wait dependence. The complete law declares all response coefficients together with time-valued tau, addressing prior compilation failures from undeclared coefficients. This is a parsimonious testable candidate, not evidence that the exponential kernel is uniquely identified or meets the RMSE threshold.","scientific_change":"Replace the inadequate u,h-only linear model with a complete shared affine response in current drive, wait, and an exponentially age-weighted prior-drive summary. All parameters are fit on the original fit rows only. The proposed paired pulse experiment tests age weighting and its change with waiting time; no claim of threshold acceptance is made."}
